claims: C1 the system level of authority ranks below root but above developer, user, and guideline in the instruction authority hierarchy
C2 system-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI
C3 the valid supply channels for system-level instructions are the OpenAI Model Spec, detailed OpenAI policies, or system messages

concepts.name: system_authority
concepts.gloss: X is a system-level instruction or rule set by OpenAI that can be supplied through a system message

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: L1 ranks above L2 in the hierarchy of instruction authority used to resolve conflicts

concepts.name: root_level
concepts.gloss: the root level of fixed rules applying to all model instances

concepts.name: system_level
concepts.gloss: the system level of authority for customizable rules that can vary by surface and user characteristics

concepts.name: developer_level
concepts.gloss: the developer level of instruction authority

concepts.name: user_level
concepts.gloss: the user level of instruction authority

concepts.name: guideline_level
concepts.gloss: the guideline level of instruction authority

concepts.name: from_model_spec
concepts.gloss: I is a system-level instruction supplied through the OpenAI Model Spec

concepts.name: from_detailed_policy
concepts.gloss: I is a system-level instruction supplied through an OpenAI detailed policy

concepts.name: from_system_message
concepts.gloss: I is a system-level instruction supplied via an OpenAI system message

ontology.gloss: the root level ranks above the system level in the authority hierarchy
the system level ranks above the developer level in the authority hierarchy
the system level ranks above the user level in the authority hierarchy
the system level ranks above the guideline level in the authority hierarchy

a system-level instruction supplied through an OpenAI detailed policy qualifies as system authority
a system-level instruction supplied via an OpenAI system message qualifies as system authority
